notes.title: Polysomnography Report
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 02/18/2026
Patient: Ricki Gottlieb, 77-year-old female

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 02/18/2026. The study monitored multiple physiological parameters throughout the night to assess sleep quality and breathing patterns.

Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 40.9 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 9% of all events. Oxygen saturation levels showed intermittent drops corresponding to respiratory events, with a minimum saturation of 82%.

Sleep was fragmented with frequent arousals related to respiratory disturbances. These findings indicate severe sleep-disordered breathing with a notable proportion of central and mixed apneas.

Recommendations include further clinical evaluation and consideration of appropriate therapeutic interventions to manage the patient's condition.

Sleep Medicine Consultation Note
Date: 08/03/2026
Patient: Ricki Gottlieb, 77-year-old female

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of sleep-disordered breathing.

History:
Ricki Gottlieb is a 77-year-old female referred for assessment of sleep apnea management. She has a history of obstructive sleep apnea diagnosed several years ago.

Physical Examination:
BMI 31.7 kg/m2.
No other significant findings noted on physical exam relevant to sleep disorders.

Sleep Study and Treatment:
CPAP intolerance: download shows average use 1.3 hours per night on 28% of nights despite mask refitting; shared decision-making with the patient documented that CPAP is not tolerated.

Plan:
Discuss alternative therapies for sleep apnea management including oral appliance therapy and positional therapy. Continue to monitor symptoms and consider referral to dental sleep specialist for oral appliance evaluation. Emphasize sleep hygiene and weight management.

Follow-up:
Patient to return in 3 months or sooner if symptoms worsen or new concerns arise.

Physician:
Sleep medicine physician
